item.title: Russian attacks kill six in Kyiv, other cities; expose gaps in Ukraine’s air defences
item.description: A series of powerful explosions thundered in the ‌night, as Ukraine’s air force warned of a ballistic missile threat; Several non-residential buildings and warehouses were struck in the attack, ​while parked cars ‌and office buildings were on fire in several districts, Kyiv Mayor said Russian missiles strike Kyiv killing one, wounding 13. Moscow has in recent weeks stepped up its use of ballistic missiles as it seeks to choke off Ukrainian strikes on oil facilities deep inside Russia that have caused critical fuel shortages affecting both the military and the civilian population.

item.title: Flash flood warnings strike north-east US amid wildfire smoke from Canada
item.description: Poor air quality from wildfires continues to plague New York City as several neighborhoods hit by thunderstormsSaturday is delivering a double dose of dangerous weather across the north-eastern US, with smoky skies from Canadian wildfires giving way to severe thunderstorms that have already triggered a flash flood warning as torrential rain pounds parts of the region. item.title: A former Ferrari boss has a blunt message: Your commute is more dangerous than his old job
item.description: Jean Todt spent decades around the deadliest motorsport on Earth. He was a rally co‑driver, then ran Ferrari’s Formula One team, then became president of world motorsport’s governing body. In his early years, a driver dying at the track barely made news. A former Ferrari boss has a blunt message: Your commute is more dangerous than his old job.

item.title: 'Sooner Or Later This Problem Will Be On Your Soil': Estonia Pushes Europe To Bar Russian Fighters
item.description: As Russia's war against Ukraine reshapes Europe's security landscape, Estonia is closely watching the Kremlin's next moves. In an interview with RFE/RL, Estonia's Undersecretary for Internal Security Joosep Kaasik discusses why Tallinn believes prevention is Europe's best defense. 'Sooner Or Later This Problem Will Be On Your Soil': Estonia Pushes Europe To Bar Russian Fighters.

item.title: 'We Have To Be Realists' Regarding Threats From Russia
item.description: Joosep Kaasik, the undersecretary for internal security in Estonia's Ministry of the Interior, told RFE/RL in an interview that his country takes the threat of a potential Russian attack seriously, but is also prepared to deal with the use of soft power by its Eastern neighbor. 'We Have To Be Realists' Regarding Threats From Russia.

item.title: ‘We are preserving a tradition’: how Ghana’s sensationalist film posters became collectible art
item.description: Hand-painted works are often wildly unfaithful to the movies they portray – reinterpretations that sometimes resulted in threats, insults and even physical attacks from viewers who felt dupedSitting on his porch in Teshie near Accra, Heavy J dipped a brush into red oil paint and dabbed it carefully on to his canvas – a flour sack – adding blood to a knife being wielded by a man.

item.description: China is building an increasingly sophisticated anti-stealth network, but its effectiveness may depend less on individual radar performance than on its ability to integrate, maintain and operate the wider system under combat pressure. item.title: New US Attacks On Roads, Bridges Reported As Iran Hits Back At Gulf States
item.description: US strikes on Iran widened early on July 18 from the Strait of Hormuz hotspot to multiple sites throughout central and southern Iran, including through the use of fighter jets, while Iran continued to pound US Gulf allies, as a fragile cease-fire further tattered. New US Attacks On Roads, Bridges Reported As Iran Hits Back At Gulf States.

item.title: Reopening Hormuz Strait Easier Than Restoring Confidence, Naval Analyst Tallis Says
item.description: With the US and Iran launching fresh strikes in the Middle East, the Strait of Hormuz is back under the spotlight. Naval strategist Joshua Tallis says restoring commercial confidence -- not military force alone -- will determine when shipping returns to normal. Reopening Hormuz Strait Easier Than Restoring Confidence, Naval Analyst Tallis Says.

item.description: Distillery owner could face only three months in jail over alleged poisoning of Australian teenagersGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastThe Australian government has increased its travel alert level for Laos, advising travellers to “exercise a high degree of caution” due to the risk of methanol poisoning. item.title: Ukrainians Protest For A Second Day Over Defense Minister's Dismissal
item.description: Protests spread across Ukraine on July 17, two days after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sacked the country's popular defense minister, Mykhaylo Fedorov, in a cabinet shakeup. Fedorov had reportedly clashed with Ukraine's top military leader over the country's wartime strategy. Ukrainians Protest For A Second Day Over Defense Minister's Dismissal.

item.description: Escaped flowerhorn cichlids are causing concern for native species and about parasites capable of infecting humansEscaped ornamental aquarium fish have integrated into a local ecosystem in the Philippines, but scientists say they may be threatening the native biodiversity of the lake. item.title: Ukraine Claims New Strikes On Russian 'Shadow Fleet' Tankers
item.description: Ukraine said its drones struck 159 vessels it identifies as part of Russia’s shadow fleet during a 12‑day campaign in the Black Sea Kyiv says it has hit 159 vessels linked to Russia's so-called shadow fleet during a 12-day drone campaign in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov. Ukrainian officials have said the operation is aimed at disrupting the transportation of oil and other shipments used to evade international sanctions.

item.title: Thai prisoners brew a path back to daily life
item.description: It looks like a regular coffee shop, albeit set up in an old red bus. Stairs lead up to a serving hatch, with a menu of drink options. A selection of jaunty coffee-related messages like “My one and only love: Americano” and “Miss you a latte,” adorn the side of the bus. Thai prisoners brew a path back to daily life.

item.title: UN chief calls for new diplomatic push following attacks on civilian areas
item.description: The UN Secretary-General remains deeply concerned by the continuing deadly military escalation between Iran and the United States, his spokesperson said on Friday as attacks destroyed key civilian and military infrastructure across the Gulf region.
